description_en: The Avāḥ Capāḥ belongs to the Avāle community of Cyāsal. This impressive architectural complex is located at the northern side of Bhindyaḥlāchi Square and has multiple functions. The southern part of thecapāḥ´sground floor used to be an openphalcābut now is closed off by latticework. Only one bay at the western side is accessible, leading to a Gaṇeśa shrine. The second floor is open at the southern side, and furnished with a wooden balustrade. The main deity of the monument, Bhairava, is displayed in a painting on the second floor. The sacred painting is not shown to the public and might not be photographed. At its northern side, thecapāḥhas a lower ground floor (due to the slope of the area), and thus technically has three storeys.The entirecapāḥwas dismantled and rebuilt in 1995 with the support of the German Technical Cooperation (GTZ-udle). None of the historical wooden elements were reused. In 2006 thecapāḥandphalcāwere renovated again with funding amounting to 60lākhRupees from the Lalitpur Sub-Metropolitan Office.The famous Jhyālicā Saṃkegu (shadow play) is performed annually here during Indrajātrā.
description_ne: च्यासलको भिन्द्यःलाछि चोकको उत्तरपट्टि रहेको यो दुईतले चपाः अवाले समुदायको स्वामित्वमा रहेको छ । सन् १९९५ मा जर्मन टेक्निकल कोअपरेसन (GTZ)को सहयोगमा यो चपाः भवन पूरै भत्काएर पुरानो कुनै पनि काठ प्रयोग नगरी नयाँ बनाइएको थियो । दक्षिणतर्फ फर्किएको यो फल्चा भुइँ तलामा पश्चिमतर्फको एउटा मात्र कवल गणेश फल्चामा जानको लागि बाटो छाडेर अरू सबैकाठको फलेक र आँखीझ्याल बनाई बारिएको छ । सन् २००६ मा यो फल्चाको पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो । यस फल्चामा हरेक वर्ष इन्द्रजात्राको दिन झ्यालिचा संकेगु देखाइन्छ । गणेश फल्चा सहित यो चपा बनाउनको लागि ललितपुर महानगरपालिकाले ६० लाख रूपैयाँ अनुदान दिएको थियो ।
monument_assessment: Repaired , Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)

historical_events.event_description: The entire Capāḥ was dismantled and rebuilt in 1995 with the support of the German Technical Cooperation (GTZ-udle).According to locals from the neighbourhood, the wood that was used for restoration came from a large tree that stood in front of Thalbuṃ Phalcā (LAL4150). Vegetable vendors used to sit underneath the tree: there is a myth is that everyone who touched the tree with a vegetable would then be able to sell it immediately.
